stances.claim: CJP's dissent in Manila Prince v. GSIS is his most principled economic-nationalism departure: Manila Hotel is not part of the 'national patrimony' that Section 10 of Article XII protects for Filipino citizens. The majority's treatment of a hotel as national heritage misapplied the provision and distorted the fair-competition principle. CJ Davide was CJP's co-dissenter.
stances.rhetorical_move: textual-limitation argument: the Manila Hotel case as a specific instance of economic nationalism misapplied -- the constitutional protection is narrower than the majority held
stances.confidence: asserted as CJP's own dissenting position

stances.claim: La Bugal-B'Laan is the most dramatic reversal in CJP's judicial career: he was the minority leader in the original 8-5 decision (which struck down the Mining Law), then won on MFR as ponente of the 10-4 reversal (which upheld it). The Mining Law upheld the deferential-interpretation principle that courts should not strangulate economic growth.
stances.rhetorical_move: dramatic-reversal-as-philosophical-vindication: leading the minority and then winning the MFR as ponente as the definitive proof of the living-Constitution school's superiority

notable_anecdotes: La Bugal-B'Laan reversal: CJP was the original minority leader in the 8-5 decision that struck down the Mining Law (January 27, 2004); after a year-long MFR deliberation, he won at 10-4 and wrote the reversal as ponente (December 1, 2004). The most dramatic judicial reversal in his career.

Bayan v. Ermita: Justice Azcuna's ponencia unanimously struck down the Calibrated Preemptive Response (CPR) policy and reiterated the 'maximum tolerance dictum' for public assemblies -- 'expressly wrote on this [liberty-and-prosperity] philosophy in his sterling ponencia.'

The living Constitution Four: CJs Davide, Puno, Sereno and Panganiban explicitly named as the living Constitution school -- 'who believe that jurists are not mere social technicians and legal automatons; they are social engineers who courageously fix their gaze on the underlying principles and overarching aspirations of the Constitution.'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered April 18, 2013 at the Claudio Teehankee Rule of Law Award ceremony -- jointly honoring CJP and Justice Ameurfina Aguinaldo Melencio-Herrera, presented by Center Chairman CJ Hilario Davide Jr. and Executive Director Ambassador Manuel AJ Teehankee -- these closing remarks by CJP respond briefly to Justice Adolf Azcuna's lecture on SC decisions on economic provisions. On Manila Prince v. GSIS: 'Manila Hotel was not one of the rights, privileges, and concessions covering the national economy and patrimony that Section 10 of Article XII gives preference to Filipino citizens' -- CJP and Davide were co-dissenters. On La Bugal-B'Laan v. Ramos: CJP was the original minority leader in the 8-5 decision (Jan 27, 2004) that struck down the Mining Law; after a year-long MFR deliberation, he won at 10-4 (Dec 1, 2004) and wrote the reversal as ponente. On constitutional interpretation: CJP names CJs Davide, Puno, Sereno and himself as the living Constitution school -- 'jurists are not mere social technicians and legal automatons; they are social engineers who courageously fix their gaze on the underlying principles and overarching aspirations of the Constitution to nurture a free and prosperous nation' -- illustrated by the Scalia-Kennedy Global Forum anecdote. He thanks Azcuna for writing the Bayan v. Ermita ponencia (unanimously striking down the Calibrated Preemptive Response policy) which 'expressly wrote on this philosophy in his sterling ponencia,' and for being a leading member of the Panganiban Court. He thanks Metrobank Foundation (Aniceto 'Chito' Sobrepena as 'energetic president') for co-sponsoring FLP's Professorial Chairs Program, Dean Sedfrey Candelaria (a Chair Holder) and Ateneo de Manila for 'never tiring as a host of the activities of FLP.'
